research:
Usage (2025-26 Basketball-Reference; 2026-27 has no games yet): Banchero 27.6%, Jalen Johnson 27.0%, F. Wagner 27.0% (34 g), McCollum 26.9% with ATL (41 g, 25.7% overall), Alexander-Walker 23.9%, Bane 23.3%. Trae Young and Kuminga are gone from ATL, so JJ and McCollum pick up the touches.
DvP (my computation from all 1,231 ESPN 2025-26 regular-season box scores, FanDuel scoring, ESPN G/F/C groups; rank 1 = most allowed): ORL vs G 10th (114.8), F 28th, C 12th; ATL vs G 16th, F 12th, C 14th. RotoGrinders, FantasyPros and Hashtag were blocked from this session.
Only McCollum clears both gates. 93% ladder (2025-26, 76 g): 9+ pts 93.4%, 1+ reb 93.4%, 2+ ast 94.7%. ATL-only (41 g): 9+ pts 95.1%, 2+ ast 95.1%, 1+ reb 90.2%. Off the bench (16 g): 12+ pts 93.8%.
SGP: o8.5 pts + o1.5 ast + o0.5 reb. The raw product is 0.826. I shrink it to 0.75 because he came off the bench in all three preseason games (19-22 min). No SGP or alt prices were posted, so the implied ~0.87 (about -650) is the product of estimated leg prices: no edge, no highlight. A 93% three-leg version cannot get near the -200 to +300 band.
Main McCollum prop found: o16.5 pts -123 (DraftKings via SI). His ATL rate at 17+ is 63%, but bench minutes make that close to fair.
Totals (method, BBR 2025-26): pace avg (101.7 ATL, 100.0 ORL) = 100.85. ATL = avg(116.1 ORtg, 114.3 ORL DRtg) x 1.0085 = 116.2. ORL = avg(114.9, 113.7) x 1.0085 = 115.3. Total 231.5 vs DK 234.5, 3.0 under, so it misses the 4-point trigger. I still list a small Under lean because ORL is short-handed.
Score model: ATL +0.9 before home court (~2) means ORL by about 1, inside the 3.5 spread.
Injuries (ESPN, Oct 21): ORL out Jonathan Isaac (knee), Anthony Black (ankle; practiced Sunday per Rotoballer), Noah Penda (hamstring), Izaiyah Nelson (ankle surgery). Franz Wagner (shoulder) left the preseason finale and did light work Sunday; he is no longer on ESPN's list but the AP preview has him day-to-day. ATL out Mouhamed Gueye (foot fracture) and Henri Veesaar (ACL, season).
Preseason (ESPN boxes): JJ 20/7, 20/14 in 25 min; NAW 25 pts in the finale; McCollum 14, 12, 7 pts off the bench; Banchero 24 and 24 in the last two; Wagner 20/4/8 on 10/13; Bane 23 in the finale.
Coaching: ORL opens under new coach Sean Sweeney (Reuters/AP), who keeps a size-first identity. ATL's Quin Snyder runs at ~101.7 pace, top-10 last season.
History: ATL swept ORL 4-0 in 2025-26 (WagerTalk), including 130-101 on April 1.
Lines (ESPN/DK): ORL -3.5 (-102) / ATL +3.5 (-118), opened -2.5; ML ORL -148 / ATL +124 (open -135/+114); total 234.5 -110/-110 (open 232.5). SI/DK earlier had ATL +3.5 -112 and 236.5. Dimers has ORL -2.5 and 233.5; TheSpread and WagerTalk 235.5; CappersPicks 235.5.
Experts: SI ATL +3.5; WagerTalk ATL +3.5 and Over 235.5 (121-118); TheSpread ATL +3 and Under 235.5; Dimers ORL 57% (117-115); iHeart model ORL 116-114; CappersPicks ORL; ESPN BPI ORL 52.7%. Consensus: lean ATL on the spread, split on the total.
Chemistry: ATL rebuilt its guard line (McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels, Dort, rookie Kingston Flemings) around Jalen Johnson. ORL keeps Banchero, Wagner, Bane, Suggs and Carter Jr. and added Vucevic.
Most likely winner: Jalen Johnson o5.5 rebounds (93.1% in 2025-26, 10.3 rpg). Lesson applied: rebound overs on high-minute bigs and forwards hold on bad shooting nights.
